HECAP topics

Research topics of the INSPIRE-HEP literature, defined from scratch by clustering its own citation network, with no outside taxonomy: two papers share a topic when they cite each other densely. — papers in — topics and — areas, from the tables of restrepo/inspireauth10 (INSPIRE-HEP downloaded on 2026-11-09), all papers including those with more than 10 authors. The Method tab says how.

Papers per year by area

Only papers with a topic. INSPIRE's coverage changes with time: it took in most of astro-ph around 2003–2007 and much of quant-ph lately, which shows in the astrophysics and quantum physics areas.

Growing topics

Shrinking topics

Areas of a country

Share of the country's papers in each area, against the share of all papers with a topic. A paper counts for every country of its authors' affiliations.

Topics of the country

Specialization: the topic's share of the country's papers divided by its share of all papers with a topic; above 1, the country publishes relatively more in it. Topics with 30 or more of the country's papers. Click a column to sort.

How the topics were made

  • Network. Every paper of the tables is a node, the corpus of 1 to 10 authors and the collaboration papers alike; a link joins two papers when one cites the other (— links). This is the direct-citation approach of Waltman & van Eck (2012), used by CWTS for the OpenAlex topics, but nothing here is mapped to OpenAlex, arXiv or any other classification.
  • Topics. Leiden clustering (Traag, Waltman & van Eck 2019) maximizing modularity at resolution —, with igraph, up to 20 passes. Clusters under 100 papers join the cluster they share the most links with. Papers with no link (old records, theses, notes) get no topic.
  • Seeds. Leiden is randomized. Four runs with different seeds agree at NMI 0.84–0.85 and ARI 0.64–0.69 for topics; the run that agrees best with the others is kept. Small topics shift a little between runs, so their exact borders should not be over-read.
  • Areas. Leiden on the graph of topics, with the links inside each topic kept, at resolution —, the best of 50 runs; the four seeds agree at ARI 0.85–0.90.
  • Names. Each topic was named from the titles of its most cited papers (from INSPIRE), checked against its arXiv categories and journals.
  • Map. Topics are placed by a force layout of the graph of topics, each topic linked to its 6 strongest neighbours by association strength (links between two topics over the product of their total links).

Code: reproduce/topics/ of restrepo/inspireauth10, and the step log in .claude/skills/inspire-topics/SKILL.md.

Sources

Computed by reproduce/topics/ of restrepo/inspireauth10 from the tables in data/ (INSPIRE-HEP, CC0) and their citation network, clustered with Leiden (igraph 1.0, leidenalg 0.12). Built 2026-11-13. Self-contained page; d3 v7.9.0 (ISC licence) is included.

  • Totals (9 rows): Papers of the tables, papers with a topic and without one, topics, areas, citation links and the clustering resolutions. Download JSON
  • Areas (6 rows): The six areas: papers, topics, citations, arXiv mix, and papers in 2011-2015 and 2021-2025. Download JSON
  • Topics (304 rows): Each topic: name, area, papers (and those with 1 to 10 authors), citations, years, arXiv categories, journals and countries (shares), most cited papers, and its position on the map. Download JSON
  • Links between topics (1114 rows): Citation links between topics (each topic's 6 strongest by association strength), which place the topics on the map. Download JSON
  • Papers per year by topic (19152 rows): Papers of each topic by publication year. Download JSON
  • Papers per year by area (668 rows): Papers of each area by publication year. Download JSON
  • Areas by country (433 rows): Papers in each area of each country with 1,000 or more papers with a topic. Download JSON
  • Topics by country (17434 rows): Papers in each topic of each country with 1,000 or more papers with a topic. Download JSON
